acceptance_criteria: php.duplicate-mock-setup is registered and documented as a PHP-native adaptation of upstream tests.duplicate-mock-setup.
The same meaningful PHPUnit mock/stub behavior setup repeated in at least three distinct test files produces deterministic findings on the affected files.
Bare createMock/createStub declarations, tearDown-only setup, clusters in fewer than three files, and semantically different mock target or method shapes stay quiet.
php.mock-heavy-tests-without-assertions and existing finding/delta behavior remain unchanged.
No generic SLOP-13 parity fact layer, plugin system, benchmark infrastructure, or analyzer/scheduler special case is added.
composer validate --strict, composer run lint, composer run analyse, composer run test, composer run scan:self and composer run phar:build pass on the implementation head.
behavior_anchors: PHP test source -> existing file.text -> repo.testMockDuplication clusters -> php.duplicate-mock-setup finding
existing php.mock-heavy-tests-without-assertions single-file behavior remains independent
goal: Adapt upstream tests.duplicate-mock-setup into a conservative PHP rule that reports meaningful PHPUnit mock/stub behavior setup repeated across at least three distinct test files, using one focused repo-level duplication fact rather than a generic parity prerequisite layer.
non_goals: Do not add generic upstream fact-parity infrastructure or make SLOP-13 a prerequisite for this rule.
Do not port barrel-density, async-noise, plugin, benchmark, delta-strategy, or release-comparison features.
Do not change existing rule scoring, evidence, or baseline identity unless a focused compatibility fix is required and separately evidenced.
Do not treat common bare PHPUnit mock creation as duplication evidence.
